header.name: Measure and probability theory
header.description:
The first half of this course will consists of topics from measure theory, which can be considered to be a branch of mathematical analysis dealing with the foundations required to associate a notion of measure (such as volume) to subsets of a set. This study provides foundational tools for many areas of mathematics, such as Riemannian geometry, probability theory, functional analysis, dynamical systems, etc.

As a specific application, we revisit probability theory using the framework of measure theory in the second half of the course.
prerequisites_mandatory: Real Analysis - I or Math - III or equivalent

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to rigorously establish the existence of Lebesgue measure

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to work with Integrations

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to apply measure theory to understand probability theory

lecture_topics: Review of relevant topics from Analysis
Distribution functions of probability measures on R
Weak and Strong Laws of Large Numbers
Optional topic (time permitting): Ergodic theorems or Martingales

Probability and measure, by Patrick Billingsley.
Introduction to probability and measure, by K.R. Parthasarathy
Measure Theory and Probability Theory, by Krishna Athreya and Soumendra N. Lahiri
An Introduction to measure theory, by Terence Tao
